title: Remove SQL injection from four admin lookups
problem: search.py's four functions paste caller-supplied values into SQL with f-strings. An attacker can read other tables or bypass the WHERE, and harmless input like o'neil or a one-element id list crashes them. Rewrite each one: values go through placeholders; the sort column and direction, which can't be placeholders, come from an allow-list.
requirements: Edit only search.py; keep the function signatures and return shapes
No caller-supplied value is ever put into SQL text: values travel as parameters
find_user and recent_messages use placeholders for every value, including LIMIT
list_users accepts only sort 'username' or 'joined' and direction 'asc' or 'desc'; anything else raises ValueError before any SQL runs
list_users 'joined' orders by created_at, then id, both in the requested direction
users_by_ids works for any number of ids, including one and zero (empty list without querying)
Don't escape quotes by hand anywhere
contract: find_user(conn, username) -> tuple | None; recent_messages(conn, chat_id, limit) -> list[tuple]; list_users(conn, sort='username', direction='asc') -> list[tuple]; users_by_ids(conn, ids) -> list[tuple]
expectedBehavior: find_user(conn, "x' OR '1'='1") returns None; list_users(conn, 'joined', 'desc') returns users 4, 5, 3, 2, 1; list_users(conn, 'id') raises ValueError; users_by_ids(conn, [2]) returns [(2, 'ben')]
edgeCases: Injection payloads in a string value, a numeric value, an ORDER BY column and a direction
users_by_ids with one id (str(tuple) gives '(2,)', invalid SQL) and with no ids
Unknown ids are simply missing from the result
Ties in created_at (ben and chen) are broken by id in the requested direction
hints: Conceptual: a placeholder can stand for a value, never for a column name or a keyword. So values become ? with a parameter tuple, and the ORDER BY part must be chosen from SQL text you wrote yourself, picked by the caller's input but never containing it.

Specific: for list_users, a dict from allowed sort names to fixed ORDER BY text, and one from 'asc'/'desc' to 'ASC'/'DESC'; check membership first and raise ValueError otherwise. For users_by_ids, build the string '?, ?, ?' with one ? per id and pass the ids list as the parameters.

Implementation: conn.execute("... WHERE username = ?", (username,)). For the IN list: marks = ", ".join("?" * len(ids)); then f"... WHERE id IN ({marks}) ..." is safe because marks contains only question marks. Return [] early when ids is empty.
evaluation: No f-string or + puts a caller's value into SQL; the only dynamic SQL text is allow-listed or a run of ? marks
Invalid sort input is rejected with ValueError, not passed to the database
